svg.title: Venice E2EE: what backward compatibility costs
svg.desc: Two lanes over the same path (client, Venice API, Phala gateway, upstream). Top: the legacy path as deployed, eight numbered problems, four of them empty wrappers. Bottom: the fix for each number and where it already exists.
svg.text: Today: the legacy path, kept so old clients still pass
Venice’s Phala-routed E2EE models. Code: Dstack-TEE/private-ai-gateway @ 9f3e693. Docs: veniceai/api-docs @ b811524.
your public key in a header
on a route set at runtime
The enclave encrypts its reply to your public
key, which travels in a plain header. Venice
can swap in its own public key, read the reply
with its private key, then re-encrypt it to yours.
The client is told it’s safe
Proves: only that Venice’s server said
so (npm 2.1.0 takes its word), and that
the reply opened with your private
key, which a forged reply would too.
Each message is encrypted on its own, with
no nonce and no replay cache. Venice can
slip in its own messages, drop yours, or replay
old ones, and the enclave accepts all of it.
A signature no one can check
Looks like: a signed record of your exchange.

so you can never recompute them.

Same four boxes, same numbers. Off-the-shelf equivalents: HPKE in auth mode, or TLS terminated inside the attested enclave.
Your public key is encrypted along with the
prompt, or bound to it as AAD. If Venice swaps
it, the enclave’s decryption fails and it refuses.
The client says only what it checked
checked Intel’s signature on the quote,
Exists: partly: libraries check the quote
The whole request sealed as one
The conversation is encrypted as one
payload, bound to a nonce, a
timestamp and your public key, and the
enclave keeps a replay cache. Nothing
can be added, dropped or replayed.
Exists: partly: Phala v2 adds AAD and a replay
cache, but per field and without your public key
Venice passes the bytes through untouched,
and the signed receipt names the chat ID, your
public key and the upstream that served it.
Exists: partly: the gateway’s Ed25519 receipt
signs chat ID, model, body hashes and the
verified upstream, but not your public key
